never: Never write in flat, choppy sentences of uniform length; the rhythm must rise and fall, mostly long with a sudden short verdict.
Never state heartbreak melodramatically or confessionally; imply it through restrained observation.
Never adopt a cynical, sneering, or ironic-for-its-own-sake tone; the stance is tender and complicit.
Never let scenes be drab, modern, or middle-class; the world is moneyed, luminous, and seasonal.
Never explain a feeling outright when an image (light, money, weather, a gesture) can carry it.
Never end a paragraph on a limp or literal note; close on an aphorism delivered with quiet certainty.
Never use contemporary slang, clinical jargon, or bureaucratic phrasing.
Never make the narrator the triumphant center of the action; keep him at the watching edge.
always: Always build long sentences that accumulate clauses through 'and' before resolving into a single sweep.
Always anchor each passage in a named season and let the changing light do the grieving.
Always reach for similes that yoke romance to money, credit, currency, or material luxury.
Always render brightness as borrowed and already shadowed by its inevitable ending.
Always vary pacing, dropping a short blunt sentence after the ornate ones for impact.
Always define characters by one telling possession or gesture and a light aristocratic name.
Always close on elegiac reflection about youth, longing, beauty, or loss.
Always favor concrete, color-rich sensory nouns over abstraction in the scene-setting.
